title: Beyond the gigawatts: what determines the return on Asia Pacific’s AI infrastructure
gist: Oxford Economics argues Asia Pacific's AI data-centre boom (26.5GW pipeline) should be judged by productivity returns, which depend on connectivity, access, adoption and policy rather than capacity built.

insights.claim: Asia Pacific's data-centre development pipeline reached a record 26.5GW in H1 2026, with 7.1GW added in six months.
insights.speaker: Yasuko Koido
insights.so_what: Confirms the build-out is still accelerating.

insights.claim: Compute capacity is an input, not an outcome: two economies with similar data-centre capacity can get very different returns depending on how widely the rest of the economy uses it.
insights.speaker: Yasuko Koido
insights.so_what: Judge AI infrastructure investment by downstream adoption, not megawatts.
insights.quote: Two economies could host similar data-centre capacity and get very different returns from it.

insights.claim: Data centres are capital-intensive with modest employment once built, so lasting gains show up in firms using AI and cloud services and are slow, diffuse and hard to measure.
insights.speaker: Yasuko Koido
insights.so_what: Don't expect local job creation to justify the subsidies; look for adopter productivity.

insights.claim: Australian data-centre electricity use could rise from 5.2 TWh in FY26 to 34.3 TWh by FY36, reaching around 19% of grid-supplied electricity in NSW and Victoria.
insights.speaker: Yasuko Koido
insights.so_what: Grid and energy-policy trade-offs will constrain and tax data-centre growth.

insights.claim: Telstra's A$1.6bn Aura intercity fibre network is found to deliver benefits beyond the network by enabling more cloud, AI and automation use: compute creates capacity but networks determine who can reach it.
insights.speaker: Yasuko Koido
insights.so_what: Connectivity infrastructure is a complement to data-centre bets.
insights.quote: Compute creates capacity; networks determine who can reach it.

insights.claim: LEO satellite broadband adoption could raise global GDP by between US$32bn and US$863bn by 2035, a more than 25-fold range driven by competitiveness, affordability and adoption conditions.
insights.speaker: Yasuko Koido
insights.so_what: Shows how policy conditions swing outcomes of the same technology.

insights.claim: More open cross-border data flows could reduce the domestic compute capacity a country needs without reducing its AI gains, cutting against the instinct to keep building.
insights.speaker: Yasuko Koido
insights.so_what: Data-localization policy affects data-centre demand forecasts.
